STEP 1 - Scene: A small pile of raw almonds (unpeeled, in their brown shells-removed skins) on a white paper/plastic plate, photographed from above on a glass-topped surface.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a small disposable plate, roughly 17 cm in diameter (similar to a side plate, slightly smaller than 20 cm). Radius 8.5 cm, area = 3.14 x 8.5^2 ≈ 227 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Almonds (about 30 whole almonds, raw, with skins on).

STEP 4 - Area: Almonds cover roughly 40% of the plate's area (the pile spans about 60% of the plate width but is clustered in the center with gaps). Almonds: 40% ≈ 91 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height is about 1.3 cm on average (almonds are ~2.5 cm long, ~1.5 cm wide, ~1 cm thick, lying flat in a mound). Volume ≈ 91 x 1.3 ≈ 118 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bulk density for whole nuts is roughly 0.5 g/ml after gaps (almonds are about 0.6–0.7 g/ml solid, but the pile has air gaps). Using 0.5 g/ml: 118 x 0.5 ≈ 59 g. Sanity check: 30 almonds at ~1.2 g each ≈ 36 g; a modest pile of ~30–40 almonds fits that, so I'll take about 45 g as a balanced estimate (a light pile of roughly 35 almonds).

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw almonds ≈ 579 kcal/100 g. 45 g x 5.79 ≈ 261 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 35 raw almonds is roughly 40–45 g and about 250 kcal, which is plausible for what is visible. A small snack-sized portion, not a full meal.
